slides: Let's look at two useful perimeter shortcuts. They turn long perimeter questions into one line, and there's a third one in the next question.

slides.say: Here's a rectangle, ten by six. Its perimeter is two times, ten plus six, which is thirty-two.
Now cut it into two smaller rectangles, four by six and six by six.
at: four by six and six by six

slides.say: The perimeter of the first piece is two times, four plus six, twenty. The second is two times, six plus six, twenty-four. Together, forty-four. That's more than thirty-two. Why?
at: The perimeter of the first piece

slides.say: Every outside side is counted once, just like before. But the cut is a side of both pieces, so it's counted twice. The cut is six, so the pieces add up to thirty-two plus two times six, forty-four.
at: the pieces add up to thirty-two

slides.say: Now cut the same rectangle across instead, with a cut ten long. We get ten by two and ten by four.
at: Now cut the same rectangle across

slides.say: Ten by two has a perimeter of two times, ten plus two. That's twenty-four. Ten by four has two times, ten plus four. That's twenty-eight. Together, that's fifty-two.
at: Ten by two has a perimeter

slides.say: And that's thirty-two plus two times ten. This cut is ten long, and it's counted twice.
So the rule, for straight cuts like these: the pieces add up to the original perimeter plus two times each cut.
Now let's look at a notch. The border goes into the shape and comes back out. Here it's a rectangular notch, two deep.

The bottom of the notch is a horizontal segment. Slide it straight up to the top line. It keeps its length, and it fills exactly the gap in the top side. So the width is covered once, ten, just like the plain rectangle.
But the two walls of the notch have nowhere to go. They are extra. Each one is two, so the perimeter is thirty-two plus two times two, thirty-six.
A notch three deep has walls of three. So it adds two times three, six, and the perimeter is thirty-eight.

Careful, a step cut out at a corner is not a notch. Its new bottom side matches the piece of the top side that was cut away, three. Its new wall matches the piece of the right side that was cut away, two. So it adds nothing, and the perimeter stays thirty-two.
at: a step cut out at a corner

slides.say: These rules are for straight, rectangular cuts like these. You'll see the corner idea again in the next question. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next video.
